rules.title: Security deposit cap of one month's rent (AB 12)
rules.requirement: Starting July 1, 2024, most landlords may charge a security deposit of no more than one month's rent, whether the unit is furnished or unfurnished. Last month's rent counts toward the deposit; first month's rent does not.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental units in California, furnished or unfurnished.
rules.exemptions: Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total may charge up to two months' rent, if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC whose members are all natural persons.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Small-landlord exception depends on total properties/units owned statewide and ownership form.

rules.citation: Cal. Assembly Bill 12 (amending Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5)
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units
rules.conflict_note: Document cites only 'Assembly Bill 12'; Civil Code section number not stated in document. Prior limits were two months (unfurnished) and three months (furnished).

rules.title: Move-in photographs required
rules.requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of the tenancy to document its condition.
rules.coverage_conditions: New residential tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.

rules.quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.
rules.conflict_note: Document describes this as state law without giving a statutory citation.

rules.title: Pre-move-out walk-through inspection
rules.requirement: Landlords must offer tenants a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of the tenancy to identify repairs or cleaning needed, so tenants can correct issues and avoid deductions.
rules.quoted_span: Under state law, landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy to identify any items that need repair/cleaning.

rules.title: Limits on security deposit deductions
rules.requirement: Landlords may deduct only amounts reasonably necessary for unpaid rent, tenant-caused damage beyond normal wear and tear, cleaning to move-in level, and (if the lease allows) replacing personal property or furniture. They may not charge for professional carpet or other professional cleaning unless reasonably necessary to restore move-in condition.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot require a tenant to pay for, or assert a claim against the tenant or the security deposit for professional carpet cleaning or other professional cleaning services, unless reasonably necessary to return the premises to the condition it was in at the start of the tenancy, minus ordinary wear and tear.

rules.title: Return of deposit within 21 days with itemized statement
rules.requirement: The deposit or remaining balance must be returned within 21 days after the tenant vacates, with an itemized statement of deductions and copies of supporting bills, invoices, or receipts.
rules.quoted_span: If deductions were made, the landlord must give the tenant a written statement itemizing the amount of and and purpose for any security deposit deductions, accompanied by copies of documents showing charges incurred and deducted by the landlord to repair or clean the premises, including a copy of any bill, invoice, or receipt for materials or supplies deductions.

rules.title: Proof that deducted repairs were completed
rules.requirement: Starting January 1, 2025, landlords must provide proof that repairs charged against the deposit were completed.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in California where repair deductions are taken.
rules.quoted_span: Starting January 1, 2025, landlords must provide proof that necessary repairs were completed.

rules.title: Move-out photographs before repairs/cleaning
rules.requirement: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must photograph the unit after regaining possession and before repairs or cleaning they intend to deduct for, and give the photos and a written cost explanation to the tenant with the itemized statement.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in California where deductions for repairs/cleaning are taken.
rules.quoted_span: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit.

rules.title: Annual interest on security deposits
rules.requirement: For units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on the security deposit at the end of each year, plus a prorated amount if the tenant moves out mid-year.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit must be fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance; coverage criteria not stated in this document.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance (security deposit interest)
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
rules.conflict_note: Interest rate and specific code section not stated in document.
